findings.finding: The sort-direction toggle button is h-6 w-6 (24x24px) with no pointer-coarse:min-h-[44px] (or any phone treatment). /triage is a phone-reachable route the audit's own sweep exercises, so this is an interactive element below the stated 44x44 touch-target floor that the audit missed.
Filter-chip buttons (px-2 py-0.5, ~20px tall) on the same /triage toolbar as TriageSortLevel were also left untouched.
findings.suggestion: Apply pointer-coarse:min-h-[44px] or document an exemption.

findings.finding: The 'Refresh tree' icon button in the Files panel is h-6 w-6 (24x24px), unchanged by this diff. Renders on TaskDetailPage, covered by mobile-work-mode*.spec.ts, another control below the 44x44 floor the sweep missed.
The 'Copy command' button is h-6 (24px tall), used by MasterTaskCard on the Board (route /), in-scope for this audit. Not touched by this diff.
The toolbar-row height-only/width-exempt trade-off should be called out explicitly in the PR description, not just inline comments, so it isn't mistaken for a completed 44x44 pass on a future audit.

Claim under doubt: This diff makes no desktop/tablet changes — it is phone-only (<=767px). — All pointer-coarse:min-h-[44px] bumps (ViewToggle, BoardStatusFilter, ClaimFilterToggle, LeadTagFilter, DensityToggle, Inbox/Settings buttons, etc.) gate purely on (pointer: coarse), which is width-independent by this codebase's own convention (useIsCompactViewport.ts's doc comment for the terminal key bar says the same). A touch tablet or touchscreen laptop at ANY width gets these bumps too, not just a 393px phone — the 'no desktop/tablet changes' framing is inaccurate for this half of the diff, though the behavior itself (touch deserves a touch target regardless of width) is plausibly intentional and consistent with prior art.
findings.suggestion: Corrected ViewToggle.tsx's shared doc comment (the family's rationale reference) to state the width-independence explicitly; PR body carries an explicit 'Scope note on pointer-coarse:' section distinguishing the width-independent height bumps from the width-gated (useIsPhoneViewport) icon-only label removal. No code behavior change — documentation correction only, since the wider reach is intentional and desirable.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: useIsPhoneViewport() (JS) and the @media (max-width:767px) CSS block never disagree. — useIsPhoneViewport() updates via an async matchMedia change listener -> React state -> re-render, while --btn-h/--btn-min-w flip synchronously on CSS recalc. During a LIVE resize crossing 767px there is a window where the CSS variables have already flipped but the JS-selected component tree hasn't re-rendered yet (e.g. the desktop labeled cascade trigger could transiently render at phone dimensions). This is genuinely untested — A20-mobile-visual-fixes.spec.ts always sets a fixed viewport before navigation, never a live cross-threshold resize.
findings.suggestion: Acknowledged as advisory: cosmetic-only (accessible name is entirely JS-controlled, never CSS-controlled, so nothing is lost, it self-corrects on the next render) and no real-device use case resizes live across this threshold. No code change; would need a live-resize E2E harness this repo doesn't build elsewhere for the same idiom.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: CreateMenuSplitButton's icon-only aria-label always carries a real accessible name. — primaryLabel = primary?.label ?? "New" only falls back on null/undefined, not on an empty string. A malformed .shipwright-webui/actions.json entry with "label": "" would set aria-label="" on phone, which per ARIA name computation actively suppresses the accessible name rather than falling through to "New" — producing a genuinely nameless interactive element (pre-existing latent issue on desktop too, but this diff is the first place it can produce a truly nameless control rather than merely an empty-looking one).
findings.suggestion: Fixed: changed `??` to `||` so an empty string also falls back to "New"; added a unit test ("falls back to a real accessible name even when the action label is an empty string") covering it.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The 4051 passing unit tests are meaningful evidence for this diff's core new behavior (icon-only rendering, accessible name, geometry). — CreateMenuSplitButton.test.tsx and ProjectCreatePhoneMenu.test.tsx contained zero references to useIsPhoneViewport, iconOnly, or aria-label before this pass. All verification of the core behavior lived in exactly 2 E2E assertions in one spec, one browser/viewport (mobile-chromium, 393px) — the large unit-test count wasn't actually evidence for this specific change.
findings.suggestion: Fixed: added unit tests to both files (icon-only class + aria-label on phone, labeled + no aria-label off phone, empty-label fallback in CreateMenuSplitButton.test.tsx; icon-only class + accessible name in ProjectCreatePhoneMenu.test.tsx), reusing the window.matchMedia mocking pattern TaskDetailHeader.phone.test.tsx already established.
